editorial.description_en: An earth wall with afternoon sun full on it — the point where an ochre stops being a neutral and starts being a colour.
editorial.description_ja: 日のあたる土壁のような、あざやかな黄土。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.776, C 0.070, h 72.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 陽 (hi, sunlight) + 壁 (kabe, wall). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Sunlit Wall" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 陽壁. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — kare-no at ΔE00 5.1, nen-do at ΔE00 6.1, kari-ato at ΔE00 7.0. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (252°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
